title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 719-720 of the continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck has identified M_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity} (the Legendre lambda-line) with a modular scheme M'_{1,1} of elliptic curves with level-2 structure, taken modulo symmetry. Base: S of characteristic 0, with a (quasi-)elliptic curve X~/S. The three points of order 2 form a finite etale cover S' -> S of degree 3. On the previous page he defines two local systems: (299) M_0 = p_*Z_{S'}/Z_S, a twisted Z-local system of rank 2, and (300) M_1 = M_0 (x) Zhat(1) = M_0 (x) T_infty(G_m), a twisted Zhat^2 local system.

On this page he states the following. Giving the 'Fermat tower' is equivalent to giving, for every such X~/S, an M_1(X~/S)-torsor F_infty(X~/S) on S (301), compatible with isomorphisms and base change. The 'previous theorem' says such a functorial family exists. It is unique up to unique isomorphism once one requires that the induced homomorphism Pi_{0,3}^ -> M^ be the canonical one.

Modern reading: over the universal level-2 base M_{0,3}, M_1 is constant, equal to Zhat(1)^2 = Zhat(1)^3/diagonal. An M_1-torsor is therefore a pro-abelian cover with group Zhat(1)^2. The canonical one is the maximal pro-abelian (abelianization) cover of P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, i.e. the tower of Fermat curves x^n + y^n = 1, obtained by adjoining lambda^{1/n} and (1-lambda)^{1/n}. This quotient is characteristic and hence S_3-stable. So the tower descends, as a torsor under the twisted lattice M_1, to the stack of elliptic curves with no level structure (modulo +/-1). This makes the Fermat tower a 'modular' object attached functorially to any family of elliptic curves.

Second part, which begins here and continues on p. 720. Take an elliptic curve X/S. Let J be the generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht-Serre) for the reduced modulus D = S' (the 2-torsion multisection), and J^0 its degree-0 part. Then J^0 is an extension of X by the torus Res_{S'/S}G_m / G_m = G_m (x) M_0 (302). Taking Tate modules T_infty = lim of n-torsion gives 0 -> M_1 -> T_infty(J^0) -> T_infty(X) -> 0 (303). Hence an M_1-torsor is the same as a T_infty(J^0)-torsor together with a section of the induced T_infty(X)-torsor.

Grothendieck then asks whether the Fermat torsors F_infty(X/S) admit a reasonable description in terms of the geometry of X/S. The margin points to a 'geometric variant' at (320), p. 724.

Natural answer (implicit, not written here): F_infty is the Kummer (division) torsor of a canonical S-point of the torus G_m (x) M_0 inside J^0. Such a point comes from canonical units built from the 2-torsion, e.g. the values P'(e_i) = (e_i - e_j)(e_i - e_k) for a Weierstrass cubic P, modulo diagonal scaling. This recovers, up to 2-torsion sign twists, the Kummer classes of lambda and 1 - lambda. In other words, the 1-motive [Z -> J^0] realizes the Fermat tower.
errors: No mathematical error found. The identification ker(J^0 -> X) = (Res_{S'/S}G_m)/G_m = G_m (x) M_0 is right (cocharacter lattice p_*Z/Z = M_0). Exactness of T_infty in (303) holds for smooth connected commutative group schemes in characteristic 0.
Gap: the uniqueness/normalization statement ('l'iso unique pris, en exigeant ... l'hom canonique') only sketches how the torsor is rigidified, i.e. via the map Pi_{0,3}^ -> M^.
Gap: possible sign / 2-torsion ambiguities (twists of the Kummer class by -1) when descending the torsor from level-2 to the S_3-quotient are not discussed on this page.

ideas.what: P^1-{0,1,inf} as the moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 structure (Legendre lambda-line)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (M_{1,1} / M_{0,4} in the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Fermat tower as a canonical torsor under the twisted lattice M_0 (x) Zhat(1), defined functorially for every family of elliptic curves (descent from level 2 to all elliptic curves)
ideas.modern_name: Abelianization cover of P^1-{0,1,inf} (Fermat curves) as an S_3-equivariant / modular pro-abelian torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fermat curves as abelian covers of the lambda-line: classical; Galois action on Fermat-tower Tate modules: Ihara (1986), Anderson, Coleman

ideas.what: Generalized Jacobian of an elliptic curve with modulus the 2-torsion divisor, giving an extension of X by the twisted torus G_m (x) M_0, and the Tate-module sequence 0 -> M_1 -> T(J^0) -> T(X) -> 0
ideas.modern_name: Rosenlicht-Serre generalized Jacobian / 1-motive extension of E by a torus; Tate module of a semi-abelian scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht, Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes); Deligne (1-motives, Hodge III)

ideas.what: Description of M_1-torsors as T(J^0)-torsors with a section of the induced T(X)-torsor; proposal to describe the Fermat torsor via the geometry of X/S
ideas.modern_name: Kummer torsor of a point of a semi-abelian scheme (1-motive [Z -> J^0])
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kummer theory for 1-motives: Deligne; Bertolin et al.

missed.claim: The abelian (Fermat) tower over P^1-{0,1,inf} is reinterpreted as a canonical torsor attached functorially to arbitrary families of elliptic curves, under the lattice twisted by their 2-torsion. It is to be realized through the Tate module of the generalized Jacobian of E with modulus E[2] - essentially a 1-motive realization of the Fermat tower. Ihara-style studies of Galois action on the Fermat tower (Jacobi sums) do not seem to phrase it via generalized Jacobians of elliptic curves.
missed.quote: la donnée de la "tour de Fermat" équivaut à la donnée, pour les X~/S dessus, d'un torseur F_infty(X~/S) torseur sur S sous M_1(X~/S) ... Considérons J la jacobienne généralisée de X relative au diviseur de cette multisection
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a modular, 1-motivic description of the metabelian/abelian layer of pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}). This may connect Ihara's Jacobi-sum power series and the Fermat-curve Galois representations to Kummer classes of canonical units built from the 2-torsion of the universal elliptic curve (elliptic-unit-like objects).

missed.claim: The explicit question of describing F_infty(X/S) geometrically is left open here (a variant is promised at (320), p. 724).
missed.quote: Y a-t-il une description raisonnable des torseurs de Fermat F_infty(X/S), en termes de la géométrie de la courbe elliptique relative X/S ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean answer is plausible: the Kummer torsor of the point (P'(e_i))_i of the torus G_m (x) M_0, with careful treatment of sign twists. It would give an integral, level-free model of the Fermat tower over the moduli stack of elliptic curves.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are classical: the lambda-line, Fermat curves, generalized Jacobians, Kummer torsors. But tying the Fermat tower to a functorial torsor over all elliptic families via the generalized Jacobian with modulus E[2] is a neat, apparently unrecorded reformulation. It is modest rather than deep.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the struck word before 'dessus' is a crossed-out 'comme' ('[-comme-] dessus'), probably intended as 'ci-dessus'.
'Π_03^' is better read as Π_{0,3}^ (profinite fundamental group of M_{0,3}), mapping to M^ (a profinite completion of M).
Margin note reads: 'pour une variante géométrique cf (320) p. 724'.
